Viennese Apple Strudel

Served at: Magic Flute

Serves 8Prep 30 minCook 40-45 min

Indulge in the classic taste of Vienna with this delightful Apple Strudel, a perfect treat to elevate any special occasion. While not tied to a specific holiday, this elegant pastry embodies the rich culinary tradition of Austria, making it a wonderful dessert to enjoy, perhaps after an evening at the opera or a festive gathering. Its flaky crust and warm, spiced apple filling offer a comforting and sophisticated experience.

Ingredients

  • 6 medium (about 2 lbs / 900 g) tart apples, such as Granny Smith or Honeycrisp, peeled, cored, and thinly sliced
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar
  • 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) dark rum (optional)
  • 1/2 cup (70 g) golden raisins (optional)
  • 1/2 cup (60 g) plain breadcrumbs
  • 4 tablespoons (56 g) unsalted butter, melted (for breadcrumbs)
  • 12 sheets (about 1 box) frozen phyllo dough, thawed according to package directions
  • 1/2 cup (113 g) unsalted butter, melted (for brushing phyllo)
  • Powdered sugar, for dusting

Method

  1. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. In a large bowl, combine the sliced apples, granulated sugar, cinnamon, rum (if using), and raisins (if using). Toss gently to coat and set aside for 15 minutes to allow the flavors to meld and apples to release some juice.
  3. In a small skillet, melt 4 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. Add the breadcrumbs and cook, stirring frequently, until golden brown and toasted, about 3-5 minutes. Remove from heat and let cool slightly.
  4. Lay a clean kitchen towel or a large sheet of parchment paper on a clean work surface. Carefully unroll the thawed phyllo dough.
  5. Take one sheet of phyllo dough and lay it flat on the towel. Brush lightly with melted butter. Layer another sheet on top, brush with butter, and repeat until you have 6 sheets layered, each brushed with butter.
  6. Sprinkle half of the toasted breadcrumbs evenly over the buttered phyllo sheets, leaving a 2-inch (5 cm) border along the long edges.
  7. Drain any excess liquid from the apple mixture. Spread half of the apple filling evenly over the breadcrumbs, again leaving a 2-inch (5 cm) border.
  8. Starting from one long edge, carefully and tightly roll the phyllo and filling into a log using the kitchen towel to help lift and guide it. Tuck in the ends as you roll to seal the filling.
  9. Carefully transfer the strudel seam-side down onto the prepared baking sheet. Brush the top generously with melted butter.
  10. Repeat the layering, breadcrumb, and apple filling steps with the remaining 6 phyllo sheets, breadcrumbs, and apple mixture to create a second strudel.
  11. Bake for 40-45 minutes, or until the strudel is golden brown and crispy. If it browns too quickly, you can loosely tent it with foil.
  12. Remove from the oven and let cool on the baking sheet for at least 15-20 minutes before slicing.
  13. Dust generously with powdered sugar before serving warm or at room temperature.

Tips

  • Ensure phyllo dough is completely thawed and handled gently to prevent tearing. Keep unused sheets covered with a damp cloth to prevent drying out.
  • For extra richness, add a tablespoon of finely chopped walnuts or almonds to the apple filling.
  • Serve with a dollop of whipped cream, vanilla ice cream, or a warm vanilla sauce for a truly decadent experience.
